text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on September 16 in history.
1387 - Henry V, king of England from 1413, born. He defeated the French at the Battle of Agincourt two years later which led to his being regent of France.
1498 - Tomas de Torquemada, first Grand Inquisitor of Spain, died. He delighted in his office and his name has become the symbol for extreme cruelty.
1620 - The Mayflower ship, which carried Pilgrims to Plymouth, Mass., to establish the first permanent colony, set sail from Southampton, England.
1685 - John Gay, English poet, composer and dramatist, born. His most popular work, "The Beggars Opera", was the first important ballad opera.
1736 - Gabriel Daniel Fahrenheit, German physicist, died. The inventor of the alcohol and mercury thermometers, his name is commemorated by the thermometric scale.
1810 - Mexico issued the Grito de Dolores, which called for the end of Spanish rule. Mexican Independence Day celebrates this event.
1824 - Louis XVIII, King of France in title from 1795 to 1814 and in fact from 1814 to 1824, died and was succeeded by his brother Charles X.
1858 - Andrew Bonar Law, British statesman, born. He was the first British prime minister (October 1922 to May 1923) to come from a British overseas territory (Canada).

1923 - Lee Kuan Yew, politician and barrister, born. Prime minister of Singapore from 1959 until 1990, he masterminded Singapore's transformation from a colonial outpost into a booming industrial metropolis.
1924 - Lauren Bacall born as Betty Perske. U.S. film actress married to Humphrey Bogart from 1945, she starred with him in "To Have and Have Not", "The Big Sleep" and "Key Largo".
1925 - Charles Haughey, Irish politician, born. Prime minister 1979-1981, 1982 and 1987-92. His ability to shake off scandals and leadership challenges earned him the nickname "the Great Survivor".
1931 - Libyan nationalist leader, Omar Mukhtar, was captured and executed by Italian forces.
1963 - The Federation of Malaysia was formed out of a marriage of Malaya, Singapore, Sarawak and Sabah. These territories were formerly under British rule.
1966 - The new Metropolitan Opera House at the Lincoln Centre in New York opened with Samuel Barber's "Antony and Cleopatra".
1977 - Operatic soprano Maria Callas died in Paris aged 53.
1975 - Papua New Guinea gained full independence from Australia.
1978 - In Iran, 25,000 people were killed by an earthquake which measured between 7.5 and 7.9 on the Richter scale. It levelled the town of Tabas and many other villages.
1990 - The Mayor of Nice, Jacques Medecin, announced his resignation and brought to an end a right-wing dynasty which started in 1928. He had been accused of embezzlement and racism.
1991 - Liberals scored a resounding victory in first direct elections to Hong Kong's legislature, saying their triumph sent a clear message to China that the people want more democracy.
1992 - Britain announced it was withdrawing from the European Exchange Rate Mechanism.
1994 - The U.S. envoy to Somalia slipped out of Mogadishu, ending official American presence in the destroyed nation.
1994 - British Prime Minister John Major lifted media restrictions on Sinn Fein, the political wing of the IRA.
